paper_metadata.title: Microstructure evolution of high-performance Ni-base superalloy GTD-111 with heat treatment parameters

evidence.quote: The Ni-base superalloys possess high stability and strength at high temperatures and for this reason they are used in manufacturing of gas turbine hot components.
First, some cast specimens from GTD-111 ingots were obtained. The specimens were heat treated with different cycles.

The secondary /H9253′spheroids of average 0.1 /H9262m diameter are produced during aging after partial solution treatment.

The /H9253–/H9253′ eutectic is distributed at dendrite boundaries, often near micropores, showing that it is formed during the last stages of solidification.

The superalloy GTD-111 is strengthened by two main strengthening mechanisms: solid solution hardening and precipitation hardening. Elements such as: W, Mo, Ta, Ti and Cr are the most potent solid solution strengtheners.

Some factors such as: coherency strains at /H9253–/H9253′ interface, elastic moduli difference between /H9253′ and /H9253 matrix, lattice mismatch, long range ordering of /H9253′ and anti-phase boundary (APB), produced during the movement of dislocations through /H9253′ particles, strengthen the Ni base superalloys via the precipitation hardening mechanism
